classification.recommended_terminology: integral-shift criterion for an integer affine radix recurrence
classification.contextual_analogy: purely periodic repetend denominator criterion after the radix-supported denominator part has been removed
classification.attribution: Call recurrence iteration and the unit-window step elementary, and call the denominator input the multiplicative order of b modulo the denominator; Euler's totient is an available, usually nonminimal, exponent. Treat Rényi--Parry β-expansion theory only as broader historical context, not as the source of the displayed affine identity.
classification.mathematical_interest: The package is not independently novel, but it exposes an exact arithmetic interface: rational denominator information supplies persistent integral shifts, while any contradiction must come from a separate smallness, mismatch, or nonperiodicity input.
classification.reusable_scope: Integer-valued digit/carry recurrences T_(n+1)=b T_n-a_(n+1), including states outside [0,1] and digit alphabets not restricted to 0,...,b-1.
classification.why_it_matters: It organizes the #251 rational-candidate, real-tail representation, denominator removal, persistent shift, and mismatch consumers around one arithmetic interface. The alternating two-state orbit prevents denominator arithmetic or integrality from being mistaken for the hard smallness/nonconcentration input.

mechanism_comparison.standard_recurrence_arithmetic: Iterating T_(n+1)=bT_n-a_(n+1) gives T_(n+h)=b^hT_n-A_(n,h) with A_(n,h) integral.
mechanism_comparison.standard_denominator_arithmetic: For reduced denominator q coprime to b, the shift is integral exactly when q divides b^h-1; the least positive such h is ord_q(b), while φ(q) is only a universal admissible choice.
mechanism_comparison.radix_expansion_boundary: With canonical bounded digits and fractional states, the same divisibility is familiar repetend arithmetic. Those hypotheses are absent here, so expansion periodicity and uniqueness are not conclusions of this card.
mechanism_comparison.source_consumer_stack: In #251 a proposed rational sum produces exact candidate tail states; equality with the real sum identifies their real-tail casts; denominator splitting and multiplicative order produce a persistent integral shift; an adjacent small mismatch or eventual smallness plus unbounded gaps is still required for contradiction.
mechanism_comparison.local_delta: The card packages the identity, candidate representation, exact integrality equivalence, forward persistence, mismatch/open-unit-window consumers, and a sharp finite counterexample to integrality-implies-zero in one reusable interface.
